samples.summary: "keeps focus on a trigger whose menu is open" does not exercise the open-popup guard — it passes even if `hasOpenPopup()` is deleted
samples.evidence: The test clicks the Radix `DropdownMenuTrigger`, then asserts only `document.activeElement !== document.body` and `trigger.getAttribute("data-state") === "open"`. Radix portals `DropdownMenuContent` to `document.body` and moves focus into it on open, so at the deferred `setTimeout` in `toolbar-focus-release.ts:103` `document.activeElement` is the portalled menu content, which fails `el.closest(TOOLBAR_SELECTOR) !== null` (line 58) long before `!hasOpenPopup(el)` (line 60) is ever consulted. Consequently `hasOpenPopup()` — including the deliberate exact-`"open"` comparison documented at toolbar-focus-release.ts:38-49 — has no test that can fail if it is wrong or removed. The second assertion (`data-state === "open"`) is also already implied by the preceding `await screen.findByRole("menu")`, so it re-asserts Radix's own state rather than the hook's behavior. The comment in the test ("either way the trigger must not be blurred") advertises coverage the assertions do not provide.

samples.summary: No test covers the documented `data-state="on"` (Radix Toggle) case, i.e. that a pressed toggle IS still released
samples.evidence: toolbar-focus-release.ts:38-49 states the `data-state` check compares against `"open"` exactly "because `Toggle` uses the same attribute for `on`/`off` and a pressed toggle must still be releasable" — the Bold/Italic-style buttons in the real slides toolbar. The harness (toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:22-36) contains only a plain `<button>`, an `<input>` and a dropdown; no element with `data-state="on"`/`aria-pressed`. If the comparison were loosened to `startsWith`/truthiness, every pressed toggle would silently stop releasing focus and the whole reported bug (#882) would return for toggles, with the suite still green.

samples.summary: No test asserts the real slides toolbar actually carries `data-canvas-toolbar` (the hook's only opt-in)
samples.evidence: The hook is a no-op unless a rendered ancestor matches `[data-canvas-toolbar]`. The only test harness hand-writes `<div data-canvas-toolbar="">` (test file line 25), so if `<Toolbar data-canvas-toolbar="">` at index.tsx:110 lost the attribute, stopped spreading props, or the mobile branch (index.tsx:92-107, which has no attribute) were taken, no test in the repo would fail. The only slides-toolbar test found is arrange-menu.test.tsx, which does not render `SlidesToolbar`.

samples.summary: Untested branches: `role="button"` releasables, pointerdown outside the toolbar, and listener cleanup on unmount
samples.evidence: `isReleasable()` also accepts `el.getAttribute("role") === "button"` (toolbar-focus-release.ts:59) — no test renders such an element. `isPointerDrivenTarget()` returning false (a pointerdown on the canvas followed by a focus landing in the toolbar, e.g. programmatic focus) is never exercised, so the `if (!pointerDriven) return;` early-out at line 91 has no negative test other than the Tab case. The `useEffect` cleanup (lines 111-116) — which prevents a document-level listener from blurring buttons in other editors after the slides toolbar unmounts — is never asserted: no test unmounts the harness and re-checks that clicking a marked toolbar no longer releases focus.
searchedFor: grep useCanvasFocusRelease across repo for other test files

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The test at toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:50-59 asserts only (a) activeElement !== document.body and (b) the trigger's Radix-owned data-state === "open" (already implied by the preceding findByRole("menu")). DropdownMenuContent portals to document.body (ui/dropdown-menu.tsx:38-48), and Radix moves focus into the portalled content on open (trigger pointerdown preventDefault + content mount auto-focus + modal focus trap), so at the deferred callback (toolbar-focus-release.ts:103-105) document.activeElement is the portalled menu content. isReleasable then short-circuits at line 58 (closest(TOOLBAR_SELECTOR) === null) and line 59 (a div[role="menu"], not a button) before !hasOpenPopup(el) at line 60 is ever consulted. Removing or breaking hasOpenPopup — including the deliberate exact-"open" comparison documented at lines 38-49 for the Toggle "on"/"off" case — would not fail this test. Grep shows hasOpenPopup appears only at toolbar-focus-release.ts:44 and :60, and no test anywhere renders a Toggle or otherwise leaves focus on an open trigger; the Escape (61-67) and item-select (69-74) tests exercise the closed-trigger path only. So the guard branch has no test that can fail, and the test's comment ("either way the trigger must not be blurred") advertises coverage the assertions do not provide. Real and blocking under the test-adequacy rubric (vacuous test presented as coverage / untested behavior branch); none of not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope applies.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `hasOpenPopup()` (toolbar-focus-release.ts:44-49) compares `data-state === "open"` exactly, and the comment at :38-43 states this is precisely so a pressed Radix `Toggle` (`data-state="on"`) is still released. The only test for the hook (toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:22-36) renders a plain button, an input and a dropdown — no `data-state="on"` / `aria-pressed` element, and no toggle-named test. I searched beyond the reviewer's paths: the separate `packages/frontend/tests/**` suite tree (incl. tests/app/slides/toolbar/*, tests/components/menu-focus.test.ts, tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts), the harness pages (src/app/harness/interaction/page.tsx), and scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs; repo-wide grep for `toolbar-focus-release|focus-release` yields exactly one test file, and no test imports the real opted-in toolbar (`@/app/slides/toolbar`), so the hook is never exercised against real toggles either. The case is real, not hypothetical: the toolbar root that sets `data-canvas-toolbar` (app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:70,110) renders Radix Toggles in format-painter.tsx:48, insert-group.tsx:47,63, global-controls.tsx:136,151 and TextFormatGroup Bold/Italic/Underline (components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:164,182,200). The Escape test (:61-67) only pins the `data-state="closed"` value, so a loosening like `!== "closed"` or `startsWith("o")` would break every pressed toggle with the suite still green. Missing test for a documented new behavior — in-lane and major.
